job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: In a quiet classroom in Shimla, Mr. Sharma pointed at a diagram of the human eye. 'Think of the retina as a screen,' he explained to Rohan and Meera. Rohan asked, 'Does the lens change shape to focus light?' Mr. Sharma nodded, 'Exactly. In 1998, researchers confirmed that the ciliary muscles adjust the lens curvature to focus images clearly.' Meera looked at the window and noted, 'The sunlight is so bright today.' Mr. Sharma replied, 'That is why your pupils constrict to limit the amount of light entering the eye.' He added, 'This process is similar to how a camera aperture works.' Rohan then asked about the 2024 eye health survey. Mr. Sharma clarified, 'That survey focused on digital strain, not the physical anatomy of the eye.' Meera wondered if the camera controls the eye. Mr. Sharma laughed, 'No, the eye is the biological original, and the camera is the mechanical imitation.'
response.summary: Mr. Sharma explains the function of the human eye to his students, Rohan and Meera. He clarifies how the lens and pupils work to manage light and distinguishes the eye from a camera.
